nodes.subject: phone inductive power transfer
nodes.object: a driven transmitter coil, nearby receiver coil, rectification and alignment

support_spans.exact_quote: Inductive charging transfers energy through inductive coupling : alternating current passes through an induction coil , generating a fluctuating magnetic field, which creates an induced alternating electric current in a nearby secondary coil.
Charging efficiency is sensitive to lateral, longitudinal, and vertical misalignment.

accepted_phrases: Inductive charging drives a transmitter coil to create a changing magnetic field and induced current in a nearby receiver coil, and its efficiency is sensitive to lateral, longitudinal, and vertical misalignment.

nodes.subject: wireless efficiency and heat evidence
nodes.object: a general lower-efficiency mechanism and bounded tests, not a universal percentage for every pad

support_spans.exact_quote: Due to the lower efficiency of inductive charging compared to conductive charging, devices took 15 percent longer to charge when supplied power is the same amount when tested in 2018.

An amateur 2020 analysis of energy use conducted with a Pixel 4 found that a wired charge from 0 to 100 percent consumed 14.26 Wh ( watt-hours ), while a wireless charging stand used 19.8 Wh, an increase of 39%. Using a generic wireless charging pad and mis-aligning the phone produced consumption up to 25.62 Wh, or an 80% increase.
Inductive chargers produce more waste heat than wired chargers, which may negatively impact battery longevity.

accepted_phrases: The inductive-charging page reports lower efficiency, a 15 percent longer same-supply test, an explicitly amateur Pixel 4 comparison with 39 percent higher wireless wall energy and up to 80 percent with misalignment, and more waste heat that may affect longevity; these are bounded examples rather than a universal loss fraction for the frozen products.

nodes.subject: Qi delivered-power boundary

support_spans.exact_quote: It allows compatible devices, such as smartphones , to receive power when placed on a Qi charger
The control and communications unit regulates the transferred power to the level that the power receiver requests.
In 2015, WPC introduced the Qi Extended Power Profile specification which supports charging phones at up to 15 W.

accepted_phrases: Qi is an inductive standard for compatible devices, its control unit regulates transfer to the level requested by the receiver, and its Extended Power Profile supports phones at up to 15 W, so a 15 W label is not a measurement that every phone receives 15 W.
